purpose.primary: Define how 5Guides distinguishes source interpretation, modeling, formal specification, proof, compiler validation, and empirical validation.
purpose.educational: Help learners inspect exactly what a formal result establishes, what assumptions it depends upon, and what remains outside the proof.
purpose.principle: Formalization helps us say exactly what we mean, what we assume, and what actually follows.

core_questions.formal: Given these definitions and assumptions, does the conclusion follow?
core_questions.modeling: Do these definitions and assumptions represent what we intended to describe?
core_questions.empirical: Does the model adequately describe the relevant real-world evidence?

core_distinction.formal_verification: Checks consequences within an explicitly defined formal system.
core_distinction.model_alignment: Checks whether the formal representation corresponds to the intended source concept or modeled system.
core_distinction.empirical_validation: Checks whether the model is adequately supported by observations, measurements, experiments, or other relevant evidence.
core_distinction.principle: These forms of inspection may support one another but must not be collapsed into one claim.

formal_proof.interpretation: Given the supplied formal context, the conclusion follows according to the formal system.
does_not_automatically_establish: the variables correspond to measurable quantities
the source author's intent was captured correctly
another model would not work better

formalization_begins_before_proof.principle: The theorem statement and proof inherit modeling decisions made before the proof begins.

mapping_rule.principle: A valid proof at the end of a chain does not automatically validate every mapping that preceded it.
mapping_rule.inspection_target: Inspect the arrows as well as the final theorem.

questions: What did the source actually say?
What did the formal model say?
Do those correspond?
possible_transformation_errors: narrowing the source without saying so
strengthening the source without saying so
assigning a precise meaning to a source term that the source did not define
source_alignment.principle: Formalization of an existing source is also an act of interpretation.

undefined_relationships.problem: The source term may be understandable informally while lacking a unique formal semantics.
undefined_relationships.rule: Do not select a semantics merely because it makes a desired theorem provable.
undefined_relationships.interpretation: An insufficiently defined relationship may require clarification before the intended formal claim can be evaluated.

gap_preservation.principle: Formalization should expose missing precision rather than hide it.
avoid_pattern: proof is presented as though the definition came from the source

formal_questions: What type are Q, F, and S?
added_assumptions.principle: Compact notation may conceal structural assumptions that formalization forces into the open.

assumption_provenance.rule: Do not retroactively attribute assumptions introduced by the teaching model to the source.

simplification.principle: A formal teaching model may intentionally be much smaller than the source concept.
conditions: the verified result is stated narrowly
the teaching model is not presented as complete formal equivalence
simplification.example: A broader directional temperature relation may be reduced to a one-dimensional signed algebraic model for selected teaching proofs.

verification.question: Does the specified conclusion follow within the defined formal system?
verification.value: Formal verification can expose skipped reasoning steps and unsupported formal conclusions.

empirical_validation.question: Does the model adequately describe what it is intended to represent in the world?

formal_and_empirical_interaction.principle: Formalization can sharpen empirical predictions, while evidence can expose where a formal model requires revision.

compiler_success.means: The formal artifact was accepted by the compiler under the relevant formal environment.
compiler_success.principle: Compiler success should be reported at the scope at which it occurred.

possible_causes: formal model does not support the target
formal representation differs from the intended concept
compiler_failure.principle: Inspect the failure before deciding what it means.

failure_as_information.principle: A formal failure may expose an assumption, dependency, or modeling choice that was previously hidden.
failure_as_information.example_question: What assumption did I think I had?
failure_as_information.follow_up: Should that assumption actually belong in the model?

questions_after_success: Did I preserve the intended meaning?

claim_strength.preferred_question: What is the strongest claim the current structure actually supports?
claim_strength.avoid_question: What is the strongest claim I can make the proof checker accept after adding enough assumptions?

assumptions_as_result_context.principle: The assumptions remain part of the meaning of the result.
assumptions_as_result_context.warning: Reporting only D may erase the conditions under which D was proved.

types.principle: Type selection is part of modeling.
types.consequence: Different representations support different operations and preserve different information.

signed_representation_example.problem: A directional value may require negative as well as positive values.
signed_representation_example.Nat_limitation: Natural numbers do not represent negative values.
signed_representation_example.principle: A type may clarify or obscure important structure in the modeled relationship.

precision_cost.principle: Formal precision may require definitions for structures that informal language leaves implicit.

formalization_depth_rule.principle: Know which layer the current artifact has actually reached.

lean_context.example_shape: theorem result (h1 : A) (h2 : B) : C := by ...
lean_context.interpretation: Lean checks whether C follows under the supplied formal context.
lean_context.lean_does_not_independently_check: Where A and B came from or whether they are empirically true.

compiler_provenance.reason_to_record_environment: Formal tooling, libraries, theorem names, imports, tactics, and dependencies may change over time.

reproducibility.principle: A useful formal artifact should make it reasonably possible for another person to repeat the formal check.
reproducibility.question: Does this still compile under the stated or current environment?

lean_verified_language.preferred_meaning: Lean accepted the formal theorem and proof under the stated formal environment.
lean_verified_language.avoid_upgrade: Lean verified the complete real-world interpretation behind the theorem.
lean_verified_language.principle: Use verification language at the scope actually checked.

tft.boundary: Does not prove TFT's broader physical claims.

nawderian_theorem.source: Declared dimension groups and wrapping language
nawderian_theorem.boundary: Does not define wrapping unless a separate relation is supplied.

temperature_engine.boundary: Does not prove the broader physical interpretation.

unified_resonance.boundary: Does not prove that the source factors naturally form that algebra.

rtt.boundary: Does not formalize or validate the complete RTT specification.

formalization_boundaries.principle: A limitation can define exactly where the current model stops and where future work could begin.
formalization_boundaries.warning: A boundary is not automatically a defect requiring immediate repair.

complexity_rule.question: Is the current formal model sufficient for the specific claim it is intended to demonstrate?
complexity_rule.if_yes: The model may appropriately remain small.

questions: Which definitions came from the source?
Which were introduced by the teaching model?
Which assumptions are explicit?
Which assumptions might still be hidden?
What does the theorem prove?
What remains unresolved?
student_inspection.purpose: Make formalization itself into learning material.

symbols_and_precision.principle: Mathematical-looking notation is not automatically precise.

technical_language.principle: When formalization selects one meaning for a familiar word, record that choice rather than pretending the word always meant exactly that.

semantic_drift.risk: The label remains while theorem meaning changes.
semantic_drift.response: Preserve definition history when semantic change affects the interpretation of formal results.

versioning.principle: Version meaning when a definition changes enough to alter theorem semantics.
versioning.purpose: Allow later readers to determine which definition a theorem used.

explanatory_clarity.principle: Formal correctness and understandable explanation can coexist.
explanatory_clarity.question: What is this model trying to say?
explanatory_clarity.warning: If the answer disappears entirely beneath formal machinery, an explanatory layer may still be needed.

questions: Which proofs survive?
Which proofs fail?
Which fail for structural reasons?
Which fail because tooling changed?
continuity_of_formal_models.purpose: Distinguish conceptual continuity from implementation continuity.

risks: weaker theorem substituted for requested theorem
ai_and_formalization.principle: The compiler checks the formal artifact; the human still checks the intended meaning.

questions: What did the source actually state?
What did the formal model actually define?
What assumptions are present?
Does the formal representation correspond to the source?
Do variables, operations, and relationships map appropriately?
Do the conclusions follow from the supplied definitions and assumptions?
Are those assumptions mutually compatible?
Can source material be distinguished from modeling choices?
Can assumptions be distinguished from proof results?
Can limitations be seen?
What changed as the idea moved from source to interpretation to formalization to proof to revision?
What persisted?

questions.alignment: Does the formal theorem correspond to the original claim?
questions.coherence: Does the conclusion follow under the declared assumptions?
questions.clarity: Are the assumptions, model, and proof boundary visible?
questions.continuity: Did the claim change between the original statement and the verified theorem?

student_formalization_habit: To go further, I would need...

must: Distinguish formal verification from modeling and empirical validation.
Treat formal proofs as conditional on their definitions and assumptions.
Treat type selection as a modeling decision.
Report compiler validation at the scope actually checked.
Preserve formalization boundaries and unresolved definitions.
Distinguish semantic change from merely syntactic change.
must_not: upgrade compiler success into empirical validation
present a teaching abstraction as a complete formalization without evidence
invent semantics for an undefined source relationship merely to make a proof work
attribute model-added assumptions to the source
report a theorem without its materially relevant assumptions
treat mathematical notation alone as a formal definition
assume a proof remains semantically equivalent after definitions change

do_not_infer: specific experimental support not represented in the source
formal assumptions not explicitly supplied by the model
